title: Confluence min-score threshold recalibration (XAUUSD historical evidence)

hypothesis.objective: Determine whether MAST confluence's live confluence_min_score=70 threshold is well-calibrated, given a live diagnostic (2026-08-15, see QUALIFICATION_DIAGNOSTICS_NOTE.md) found zero approvals across all 4 symbols for 9+ consecutive tracked days, with 82% of rejections at exactly this gate.
hypothesis.theoretical_rationale: engine/confluence_backtest.py (new, additive this cycle) replayed engine/backtest.py's own trade_list through engine.confluence.analyze() at each signal's historical decision point -- something that had never been done anywhere in this codebase; backtest.py only ever used Layer 1 (signals.py), never MAST confluence. Over 416 XAUUSD 15m trades (2023-09-13 to 2025-09-30), expectancy is NOT monotonic in confluence score: min_score=50-55 outperforms the live default of 70 on BOTH expectancy (+0.30R / +0.31R vs +0.24R) AND trade count (161-171 vs 86), while min_score>=75 collapses expectancy toward zero (+0.14R at 75, +0.06R at 80, +0.005R at 85) despite being the 'highest quality' bucket by the score's own definition. This is the opposite of what a well-calibrated quality score should show, and suggests the live threshold may be cutting into the score's OWN sweet spot rather than filtering toward it.
hypothesis.expected_benefit: If confirmed via walk-forward (out-of-sample) testing, lowering confluence_min_score toward 50-55 could resolve the current zero-approval condition (restoring trade flow) while IMPROVING historical expectancy, not merely trading quality for quantity.
hypothesis.implementation_scope: engine/confluence_backtest.py (new, additive, 1601-test suite unaffected) -- no production code, config default, or live decision path changed. This experiment is diagnostic only; touching confluence_min_score live is a separate, later, deliberate decision requiring walk-forward evidence and explicit platform-owner sign-off, per RESEARCH_VALIDATION_SPECIFICATION.md Sec.1's governing principle.
dependencies: data/XAU_15m_data.csv (XAUUSD only -- WTIUSD/BTCUSD/EURUSD not locally available, entirely untested by this experiment)
risks: Single-symbol (XAUUSD only), single continuous in-sample window -- no walk-forward/out-of-sample split has been run yet; this is historical_testing-stage evidence only, per the Day 9 lifecycle it must still pass walk_forward_testing before paper_trading is warranted.
backtest.py's own disclosed limitations apply unchanged -- no slippage or session-conditioned spread modeling (RESEARCH_VALIDATION_SPECIFICATION.md Sec.4/14 item 1).
This comparison excludes portfolio_risk.evaluate() entirely -- live results will differ once portfolio-level gates (drawdown protection, correlation, session limits) are layered back on.

confluence.analyze() re-derives Layer 1 internally at signals.WATCH_THRESHOLD (55) vs backtest.py's own signal at signals.PUBLISH_THRESHOLD (70) -- disclosed methodology note; empirically 0 of 416 replayed trades showed a direction/entry mismatch on this dataset, so it was not a practical issue here, but is not guaranteed to hold on other symbols/periods.

The n=85-threshold bucket (n=18) falls below the 30-trade sufficiency floor (evidence_tiers.MIN_N_FOR_TRUST) -- its near-zero expectancy figure is directionally suggestive, not independently trustworthy at that n.
measurable_success_criteria: A walk-forward (expanding-window, out-of-sample) evaluation at confluence_min_score=55 shows OOS expectancy >= +0.20R with n>=30 OOS trades (a deliberately conservative bar below this in-sample result's +0.30R, since in-sample results typically overstate OOS performance).

Trade frequency at the lower threshold is high enough to resolve the current zero-approval condition without increasing max historical drawdown beyond roughly the -12R figure already on record for the current live threshold's own recent window (RESEARCH_VALIDATION_SPECIFICATION.md Sec.9.1).
rollback_criteria: OOS expectancy at the proposed threshold is not clearly better than or comparable to the current live threshold's own OOS expectancy.
OOS max drawdown materially worsens versus current live behavior.
The effect does not replicate on a second symbol once WTIUSD/BTCUSD/EURUSD historical data becomes available for this same replay.

notes: engine/confluence_backtest.py designed: replay backtest.py's own trade_list through confluence.analyze() at each signal's historical decision point; derive would-qualify per threshold post-hoc from one analyze() pass per trade. Reuses backtest.summarize() unmodified for aggregation.
engine/confluence_backtest.py built, additive, 18 tests (tests/test_confluence_backtest.py), full suite 1601/1601 passing. No production code path touched.

engine/confluence_backtest.py run against real XAUUSD 15m data (data/XAU_15m_data.csv), 2023-09 to 2025-09, 416 backtested trades, 100% replay success (0 mismatches/errors). See CONFLUENCE_BACKTEST_EXPERIMENT_NOTE.md for full findings. STOPPING HERE per this Item's own scope -- walk_forward_testing is explicitly the next stage, not run this cycle. No live config touched.

evidence.key_finding: Expectancy is non-monotonic in confluence score -- the 50-55 bucket outperforms the live 70 default on both expectancy and trade count, while >=75 collapses toward zero edge. Recommendation: run walk-forward testing at min_score=55 before any live config change.
